name: audio/3gpp
description:
The 3GP container is the multimedia file format 3GPP defined for mobile networks, registered by RFC 3839 and specified in 3GPP TS 26.244. It is a variant of the ISO base media file format, the same structure underneath MP4, trimmed to the codecs handsets were expected to carry.

`audio/3gpp` labels a 3GP file whose contents are audio only, most often AMR or AMR-WB speech from a phone's voice recorder. The same container holding video as well is [video/3gpp](/video/3gpp).

The counterpart from the CDMA2000 side of the industry is [audio/3gpp2](/audio/3gpp2).

furtherReading.title: RFC 3839 - MIME Type Registrations for 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Multimedia files

name: audio/32kadpcm
description:
32 kbit/s ADPCM is the toll-quality speech coding of ITU-T G.726, registered as a media type by RFC 3802 after first appearing in the voice profile for internet mail in RFC 2421. Adaptive differential PCM codes the difference between successive samples rather than the samples themselves, halving the bitrate of G.711 with no perceptible loss on speech.

It is the coding behind voice messaging systems of that era. The `.726` extension names the ITU-T recommendation rather than the media type.

ADPCM in a RIFF wrapper is [audio/adpcm](/audio/adpcm).

furtherReading.title: RFC 3802 - Toll Quality Voice - 32 kbit/s Adaptive Differential Pulse Code Modulation (ADPCM) MIME Sub-type Registration

name: audio/amr
description:
AMR (Adaptive Multi-Rate) is the narrowband speech codec 3GPP adopted for GSM and UMTS telephony. RFC 4867 registers both its file storage format and its RTP payload format. It codes 8 kHz speech at eight bitrates between 4.75 and 12.2 kbit/s and moves between them as radio conditions change.

Voice recorder apps on feature phones wrote `.amr` files by the million, which is why the extension long outlived the networks it was designed for. The wideband version is [audio/amr-wb](/audio/amr-wb).

IANA spells this type `audio/AMR`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4867 - RTP Payload Format and File Storage Format for the Adaptive Multi-Rate (AMR) and Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband (AMR-WB) Audio Codecs

name: audio/amr-wb
description:
AMR-WB (Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband) extends AMR to a 16 kHz sampling rate, roughly doubling the coded bandwidth. It is standardised as ITU-T G.722.2 and 3GPP TS 26.190, and shares RFC 4867 with narrowband AMR for its storage and RTP payload formats.

That extra bandwidth is what stops a call sounding like a telephone, and it is the codec behind most first-generation HD Voice. Its successor in 3GPP is [audio/evs](/audio/evs).

IANA spells this type `audio/AMR-WB`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4867 - RTP Payload Format and File Storage Format for the Adaptive Multi-Rate (AMR) and Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband (AMR-WB) Audio Codecs

name: audio/asc
description:
An `audio/asc` object is a bare AudioSpecificConfig, the MPEG-4 Audio structure that tells a decoder which coding tool, sampling rate and channel layout a stream uses. RFC 6295 registered it so that configuration could be fetched separately rather than carried inline with the audio.

Its only defined use is configuring an `audio/mpeg4-generic` RTP stream in rtp-midi mode, which is why it travels over HTTP or SMTP rather than sitting in a media file.

The registration gives `.acn` as the file extension, not `.asc`.

furtherReading.title: RFC 6295 - RTP Payload Format for MIDI

name: audio/atrac3
description:
ATRAC3 is the third generation of Sony's Adaptive TRansform Acoustic Coding, the family that started in MiniDisc. It codes stereo at 66, 105 or 132 kbit/s and carried Sony's Connect music store, the Walkman line and the PSP.

RFC 5584 defines the RTP payload format for the whole ATRAC family and registers this media type. The later variants are [audio/atrac-x](/audio/atrac-x) and [audio/atrac-advanced-lossless](/audio/atrac-advanced-lossless).

IANA spells this type `audio/ATRAC3`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5584 - RTP Payload Format for the Adaptive TRansform Acoustic Coding (ATRAC) Family

name: audio/atrac-advanced-lossless
description:
ATRAC Advanced Lossless stores a lossy ATRAC stream together with a correction layer that restores the original samples exactly. A player that understands only the lossy part still decodes the file; one that understands all of it reconstructs the source bit for bit.

That hybrid let a single file serve both a portable player and an archive copy. RFC 5584 registers it with the rest of the ATRAC family, alongside [audio/atrac3](/audio/atrac3) and [audio/atrac-x](/audio/atrac-x).

IANA spells this type `audio/ATRAC-ADVANCED-LOSSLESS`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5584 - RTP Payload Format for the Adaptive TRansform Acoustic Coding (ATRAC) Family

name: audio/atrac-x
description:
ATRAC-X is the media type for ATRAC3plus, Sony's revision of ATRAC3 that roughly doubles coding efficiency and stays usable near 64 kbit/s. It was the default on later Walkman players, the PSP and Hi-MD MiniDisc.

RFC 5584 defines the RTP payload format for the ATRAC family and registers this type. The earlier generation is [audio/atrac3](/audio/atrac3).

IANA spells this type `audio/ATRAC-X`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5584 - RTP Payload Format for the Adaptive TRansform Acoustic Coding (ATRAC) Family

name: audio/dls
description:
DLS (Downloadable Sounds) is the MIDI Manufacturers Association format for shipping the instrument samples a MIDI sequence expects, so a score is not left to whatever synthesiser the playback device happens to have. RFC 4613 registers the media type.

A DLS file holds wavetable samples together with the articulation data that maps them across the keyboard. Bundling one with a sequence for handsets is what [audio/mobile-xmf](/audio/mobile-xmf) does.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4613 - Media Type Registrations for Downloadable Sounds for Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI)

name: audio/evrc
description:
EVRC (Enhanced Variable Rate Codec) is the CDMA speech codec 3GPP2 standardised as C.S0014. It picks a rate frame by frame between full, half and eighth rate, spending bits on speech and almost none on silence, which is how CDMA networks fitted more calls onto a carrier.

RFC 4788 registers the storage format for the EVRC family. Its later members are [audio/evrcb](/audio/evrcb), [audio/evrcwb](/audio/evrcwb) and [audio/evrcnw](/audio/evrcnw).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRC`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4788 - Enhancements to RTP Payload Formats for EVRC Family Codecs

name: audio/evrc-qcp
description:
This is EVRC speech stored in QCP, the RIFF-based file format Qualcomm defined for vocoder data. RFC 3625 registers QCP together with the media types for the codecs carried inside it.

QCP is how CDMA handsets saved voice memos and how vocoder test vectors were exchanged. The bare storage format without the wrapper is [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc), and the same wrapper around the SMV vocoder is [audio/smv-qcp](/audio/smv-qcp).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRC-QCP`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3625 - The QCP File Format and Media Types for Speech Data

name: audio/evrcb
description:
EVRC-B is the second generation of the CDMA Enhanced Variable Rate Codec, standardised by 3GPP2 as C.S0014-B. It keeps the variable-rate structure of the original but adds finer control over the average rate, so an operator can trade capacity against voice quality across a wider range.

RFC 5188 registers this media type alongside the wideband EVRC-WB. The narrowband original is [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRCB`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5188 - RTP Payload Format for the Enhanced Variable Rate Wideband Codec (EVRC-WB) and the Media Subtype Updates for EVRC-B Codec

name: audio/evrcnw
description:
EVRC-NW is the narrowband-wideband member of the CDMA EVRC family from 3GPP2. One stream can carry narrowband or wideband frames and switch between them mid-call, so a handset moving through changing coverage degrades smoothly instead of being handed to a different codec.

RFC 6884 defines its RTP payload format and registers this media type. It follows [audio/evrcb](/audio/evrcb) and [audio/evrcwb](/audio/evrcwb).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRCNW`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 6884 - RTP Payload Format for the Enhanced Variable Rate Narrowband-Wideband Codec (EVRC-NW)

name: audio/evrcwb
description:
EVRC-WB is the wideband member of the CDMA EVRC family, taking the codec to a 16 kHz sampling rate for noticeably clearer speech than the narrowband original. It is standardised by 3GPP2 as C.S0014-C.

RFC 5188 defines its RTP payload format and registers this media type, and in the same document updates the subtypes for EVRC-B. The narrowband original is [audio/evrc](/audio/evrc).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVRCWB`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 5188 - RTP Payload Format for the Enhanced Variable Rate Wideband Codec (EVRC-WB) and the Media Subtype Updates for EVRC-B Codec

name: audio/evs
description:
EVS (Enhanced Voice Services) is the 3GPP codec introduced in Release 12 for voice over LTE, specified in 3GPP TS 26.441 and TS 26.445. It covers narrowband through fullband speech at rates from 5.9 to 128 kbit/s, and unlike earlier telephony codecs it handles music without falling apart.

It carries most VoLTE HD Voice, and includes an AMR-WB interoperable mode so calls reaching older networks need no transcoding. Its predecessor is [audio/amr-wb](/audio/amr-wb).

IANA spells this type `audio/EVS`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

name: audio/ilbc
description:
iLBC (internet Low Bitrate Codec) codes narrowband speech at 13.33 or 15.2 kbit/s in independent frames. Because no frame depends on the one before it, a lost packet damages only what it carried instead of corrupting the decoder state that follows, which made it a common choice for VoIP over lossy links.

RFC 3952 defines its RTP payload format and registers this media type; the codec itself is specified in RFC 3951. The general-purpose codec that replaced it is [audio/opus](/audio/opus).

IANA spells this type `audio/iLBC`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3952 - Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) Payload Format for internet Low Bit Rate Codec (iLBC) Speech

name: audio/l16
description:
L16 is uncompressed 16-bit linear PCM, big-endian, as carried in the RTP profile for audio and video conferences. RFC 4856 registers it with the other payload formats in that profile. It defaults to 8 kHz mono, with rate and channel count set by media type parameters rather than by any header inside the data.

There is no container here at all: the payload is nothing but samples. PCM wrapped with a header that describes it is [audio/vnd.wav](/audio/vnd.wav).

IANA spells this type `audio/L16`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 4856 - Media Type Registration of Payload Formats in the RTP Profile for Audio and Video Conferences

name: audio/matroska
description:
Matroska is the open container format specified by RFC 9559, built on EBML, a binary encoding that behaves like a typed and length-prefixed XML. `audio/matroska` labels a Matroska file holding audio only, conventionally saved as `.mka`.

The container is codec-agnostic and carries chapters, attachments and any number of selectable tracks, which is why WebM was derived from it. Before RFC 9559 gave it a registration the format circulated as [audio/x-matroska](/audio/x-matroska).

furtherReading.title: RFC 9559 - Matroska Media Container Format Specification

name: audio/mhas
description:
MHAS (MPEG-H Audio Stream) is the self-contained packet format for MPEG-H 3D Audio, defined in ISO/IEC 23008-3. Each stream carries the configuration needed to decode it alongside the audio itself, so a receiver can join partway through without a separate setup channel.

That property is why MHAS is the form MPEG-H takes in broadcast, where it provides next-generation audio for ATSC 3.0 and DVB. The same content packaged in an MP4 container is [audio/mp4](/audio/mp4).

name: audio/midi-clip
description:
A MIDI Clip File carries MIDI 2.0 data, the first substantial revision to MIDI since 1983. MIDI 2.0 widens 7-bit values to as much as 32 bits, adds per-note controllers, and makes the protocol bidirectional so devices can negotiate what they support instead of assuming.

The MIDI Association specifies the format as M2-116-U, version 1.0 of June 2023. It uses the `.midi2` extension to keep it distinct from the original [audio/midi](/audio/midi).

name: audio/mobile-xmf
description:
Mobile XMF is a profile of the Extensible Music Format aimed at handsets, registered by RFC 4723. XMF packages a MIDI sequence together with the DLS instrument bank it expects into one file, so a ringtone sounds the same everywhere rather than depending on each device's built-in synthesiser.

That bundling is the entire point of the format. The two parts it contains are [audio/midi](/audio/midi) and [audio/dls](/audio/dls).

furtherReading.title: RFC 4723 - Registration of Media Type audio/mobile-xmf

name: audio/prs.sid
description:
A PSID file holds music for the SID chip, the three-voice synthesiser in the Commodore 64. Instead of sampled audio it stores the 6502 machine code that drives the chip's registers, so playing one means emulating the processor and the SID together.

That is why a few kilobytes can hold several minutes of music, and why the tens of thousands of tunes collected by the demoscene remain playable today. The type sits in IANA's personal tree, which is what the `prs.` prefix marks.

name: audio/smv
description:
SMV (Selectable Mode Vocoder) is the CDMA speech codec 3GPP2 standardised as C.S0030. Its design goal was to let an operator choose a working point between network capacity and voice quality by selecting one of several modes, rather than committing to one trade at deployment time.

RFC 3558 defines the RTP payload format for SMV and for the EVRC codecs, and registers this media type. Wrapped in Qualcomm's QCP file format it becomes [audio/smv-qcp](/audio/smv-qcp).

IANA spells this type `audio/SMV`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3558 - RTP Payload Format for Enhanced Variable Rate Codecs (EVRC) and Selectable Mode Vocoders (SMV)

name: audio/smv-qcp
description:
This is SMV speech stored in QCP, the RIFF-based container Qualcomm defined for vocoder data, registered by RFC 3625 along with the other codecs carried in it.

The `.qcp` extension is shared with [audio/evrc-qcp](/audio/evrc-qcp), because the wrapper is identical and only the vocoder inside differs. The bare SMV storage format is [audio/smv](/audio/smv).

IANA spells this type `audio/SMV-QCP`. Media type names are case-insensitive under RFC 2045 section 5.1, so the lowercase form used here is the same type.

furtherReading.title: RFC 3625 - The QCP File Format and Media Types for Speech Data

name: audio/sofa
description:
SOFA (Spatially Oriented Format for Acoustics) stores head-related transfer functions and room impulse responses: measurements of how a sound changes on its way to a listener depending on the direction it came from. Binaural renderers read them to place a sound in space over ordinary headphones.

The format is standardised as AES69 and built on netCDF, so a file carries self-describing multidimensional arrays together with the geometry of the measurement rig that produced them.

name: audio/sp-midi
description:
Scalable Polyphony MIDI constrains General MIDI so a sequence degrades predictably on a device that cannot sound every voice at once. The composer marks which notes matter most, and a synthesiser short of polyphony drops the others in a defined order instead of arbitrarily.

It was written for mobile phones, and the MIDI Manufacturers Association specifies it as RP-034, published December 2001. It shares the `.mid` extension with ordinary [audio/midi](/audio/midi).

name: audio/usac
description:
USAC (Unified Speech and Audio Coding) is defined in ISO/IEC 23003-3. It puts a speech coder and a general audio coder in one design and switches between them as the signal changes, so material mixing voice and music stays efficient instead of suffering whichever tool was the wrong choice.

Sold as xHE-AAC, it stays usable well below 32 kbit/s, which is why streaming services reach for it on low-bandwidth tiers. The registration gives `.loas` as the preferred extension. In an MP4 container the same coding appears as [audio/mp4](/audio/mp4).
